learning_outcomes.text: Students are familiar with the basic concepts of electrical engineering.
Students master the mathematical apparatus required for description and can apply it to simple electrical engineering problems.
Students have the ability to analyze simple linear and nonlinear circuits with DC excitation and can consider the temperature dependence of resistive two-terminal networks.
Students know the description of the essential conversions of electrical energy into other forms of energy and vice versa.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts (electrical charge, forces on charges, field strength, voltage, potential, current)
Processes in DC networks (basic concepts and laws, basic circuit, Kirchhoff's laws, superposition principle, two-pole theory, nodal voltage analysis)
Accompanying exercises for the lecture with special consideration of mechatronics
Accompanying practical course for the lecture with special consideration of mechatronics
